scenes.heading: Roles & Template Folders (Part 2 of 2)
scenes.narration: Templates. Roles & Template Folders (Part 2 of 2). In this video we review 4 key concepts you need to know for the certification.

scenes.question: What is the default group that must be assigned so authors can create templates in a new folder?
scenes.heading: The template-authors group
scenes.body: In addition to standard authoring permissions, you need to assign group(s) and define required ACLs for authors to create templates in a new folder — the template-authors group is the default group that needs to be assigned.

scenes.question: What is the global folder in the Templates console?
scenes.heading: The default folder for templates; it also acts as a fallback if no policies or template types are found in the current folder
scenes.body: The global folder is the default folder for templates in a standard AEM instance, holding default templates and acting as a fallback if no policies and/or template types are found in the current folder.

scenes.question: What is the recommended best practice for organizing customized templates?
scenes.heading: Create a new folder rather than use the global folder, since folders must be created by a user with admin rights
scenes.body: It is best practice to create a new folder to hold your customized templates and not use the global folder. Folders must be created by a user with admin rights.

scenes.question: What is the order of precedence for template types and policies across folders?
scenes.heading: The current folder, then its parent(s), then /conf/global, then /apps, then /libs
scenes.body: Template types and policies are inherited across all folders in this order of precedence: the current folder, parent(s) of the current folder, /conf/global, /apps, /libs. If configurations overlap, only the instance closest to the current folder is presented to the user.
